def _compute_cid(packets: list[DirectivePacket], model: str) -> str:
    """Compute a deterministic composition identity hash."""
    components = [
        f"{p.layer}:{p.name}:{len(p.text)}" for p in packets
    ]
    components.append(f"model:{model}")
    raw = "|".join(components)
    return hashlib.sha256(raw.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
==== REPLACE
def _compute_cid(packets: list[DirectivePacket], model: str) -> str:
    """Compute a deterministic composition identity hash.

    The CID must change when directive content or metadata changes. Length-only
    hashing aliases different same-length directives and corrupts provenance.
    """
    components = [
        {
            "layer": p.layer,
            "name": p.name,
            "text": p.text,
            "constraint_class": p.constraint_class,
            "domain": p.domain,
            "model": p.model,
            "tags": sorted(p.tags),
        }
        for p in packets
    ]
    raw = json.dumps(
        {"model": model, "packets": components},
        sort_keys=True,
        ensure_ascii=False,
        separators=(",", ":"),
    )
    return hashlib.sha256(raw.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]

findings.description:
`bench/cdsfl_registry/composer.py::_prune_for_coherence()` tries to reduce:
density = constraint_count / token_estimate
by deleting packet text. But `constraint_count` is fixed from policy, while `token_estimate` decreases when text is pruned. Therefore pruning increases or preserves the measured density; it cannot reduce it under the current formula.
findings.proposed_fix:
<<<< SEARCH bench/cdsfl_registry/composer.py
def _prune_for_coherence(
    packets: list[DirectivePacket],
    policy: dict[str, Any],
    budget: float,
) -> tuple[list[DirectivePacket], list[str]]:
    """Prune SOFT content if constraint density exceeds budget.

    Two-pass strategy:
    1. Intra-packet pruning: remove individual SOFT directives within packets
    2. Whole-packet pruning: remove entire SOFT packets if still over budget

    HARD packets are NEVER pruned. Universal is NEVER pruned.
    """
    total_chars = sum(len(p.text) for p in packets)
    token_estimate = max(total_chars // 4, 1)
    constraint_count = _count_constraints(policy)
    density = constraint_count / token_estimate

    if density <= budget:
        return packets, []

    pruned_names: list[str] = []
    mutable_packets = list(packets)

    prunable = [
        (i, p) for i, p in enumerate(mutable_packets)
        if p.constraint_class == "SOFT" and p.layer != "universal"
    ]
    prune_order = {"situation": 0, "domain": 1, "phenotype": 2}
    prunable.sort(key=lambda x: prune_order.get(x[1].layer, 3))

    # Pass 1: intra-packet pruning — trim SOFT directives within each packet
    for idx, packet in prunable:
        target_chars = max(int(len(packet.text) * 0.7), 1)
        new_packet = _prune_packet_directives(packet, target_chars)
        if len(new_packet.text) < len(packet.text):
            mutable_packets[idx] = new_packet
            pruned_names.append(f"{packet.name}::intra")

        remaining_chars = sum(len(p.text) for p in mutable_packets)
        remaining_tokens = max(remaining_chars // 4, 1)
        density = constraint_count / remaining_tokens
        if density <= budget:
            return mutable_packets, pruned_names

    # Pass 2: whole-packet pruning if still over budget
    keep_indices = set(range(len(mutable_packets)))
    for idx, packet in prunable:
        keep_indices.discard(idx)
        pruned_names.append(packet.name)

        remaining = [mutable_packets[i] for i in sorted(keep_indices)]
        remaining_chars = sum(len(p.text) for p in remaining)
        remaining_tokens = max(remaining_chars // 4, 1)
        density = constraint_count / remaining_tokens
        if density <= budget:
            return remaining, pruned_names

    return [mutable_packets[i] for i in sorted(keep_indices)], pruned_names
==== REPLACE
def _prune_for_coherence(
    packets: list[DirectivePacket],
    policy: dict[str, Any],
    budget: float,
) -> tuple[list[DirectivePacket], list[str]]:
    """Prune SOFT content only when doing so improves measured density.

    The current density metric is policy_constraint_count / token_estimate.
    Because policy_constraint_count is fixed by the merged TOML policy,
    deleting packet text can make density worse. Therefore pruning candidates
    are accepted only when they actually lower the measured density.
    """
    constraint_count = _count_constraints(policy)

    def _density(candidate_packets: list[DirectivePacket]) -> float:
        chars = sum(len(p.text) for p in candidate_packets)
        tokens = max(chars // 4, 1)
        return constraint_count / tokens

    current_packets = list(packets)
    current_density = _density(current_packets)
    if current_density <= budget:
        return current_packets, []

    pruned_names: list[str] = []

    prunable = [
        (i, p) for i, p in enumerate(current_packets)
        if p.constraint_class == "SOFT" and p.layer != "universal"
    ]
    prune_order = {"situation": 0, "domain": 1, "phenotype": 2}
    prunable.sort(key=lambda x: prune_order.get(x[1].layer, 3))

    for idx, packet in prunable:
        target_chars = max(int(len(packet.text) * 0.7), 1)
        new_packet = _prune_packet_directives(packet, target_chars)
        if len(new_packet.text) >= len(packet.text):
            continue

        candidate = list(current_packets)
        candidate[idx] = new_packet
        candidate_density = _density(candidate)
        if candidate_density < current_density:
            current_packets = candidate
            current_density = candidate_density
            pruned_names.append(f"{packet.name}::intra")
            if current_density <= budget:
                return current_packets, pruned_names

    for idx, packet in prunable:
        if idx >= len(current_packets):
            continue
        candidate = [p for i, p in enumerate(current_packets) if i != idx]
        candidate_density = _density(candidate)
        if candidate_density < current_density:
            current_packets = candidate
            current_density = candidate_density
            pruned_names.append(packet.name)
            if current_density <= budget:
                return current_packets, pruned_names

    return current_packets, pruned_names

FINDING_ID: F014

SEVERITY: 0.70

FLAW_CLASS: 4

ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.35

FIND:  
`bench/cdsfl_registry/composer.py::_load_domain_directive()` silently fails to load existing domain variant files when the directory name differs from the filename prefix.

Location:

```python
def _load_domain_directive(
    domain: str, variant: str | None = None
) -> DirectivePacket | None:
    """Load a domain-specific directive (Layer 2)."""
    domain_dir = DIRECTIVES_DIR / domain
    if not domain_dir.exists():
        return None

    if variant:
        path = domain_dir / f"{domain}_{variant}.txt"
    else:
        txt_files = sorted(domain_dir.glob("*.txt"))
        if not txt_files:
            return None
        path = txt_files[0]

    if not path.exists():
        return None
```

Evidence from the artifact directory listing:

- Directory: `directives/product-engineering/`
- Existing file: `product_automotive.txt`
- Current constructed path for `domain="product-engineering", variant="automotive"`:
  `product-engineering/product-engineering_automotive.txt`
- That constructed file does not exist, so `_load_domain_directive()` returns `None`.

Concrete failing input:

```python
_load_domain_directive("product-engineering", variant="automotive")
```

Expected output:

```python
DirectivePacket(
    layer="domain",
    name="product_automotive",
    text=<contents of product_automotive.txt>,
    ...
)
```

Actual output:

```python
None
```

The same mechanism affects `cross-domain`, whose files are named `cross_*.txt`, not `cross-domain_*.txt`.

FOLLOW:  
The failure crosses the public `compose()` interface.

Execution path:

1. Caller invokes:

   ```python
   compose(
       task_domain="product-engineering",
       model="opus_4_6",
       domain_variant="automotive",
       review_target="..."
   )
   ```

2. `compose()` calls:

   ```python
   domain_packet = _load_domain_directive(task_domain, variant=domain_variant)
   ```

3. `_load_domain_directive()` constructs:

   ```python
   DIRECTIVES_DIR / "product-engineering" / "product-engineering_automotive.txt"
   ```

4. That path does not exist, so `_load_domain_directive()` returns `None`.

5. `compose()` simply skips the domain layer:

   ```python
   if domain_packet:
       packets.append(domain_packet)
   ```

6. The returned `ComposedDirectiveSet` still appears valid:
   - universal packet present,
   - situation packet may be present,
   - policy loaded,
   - monotonicity check runs,
   - CID and manifest are generated.

Downstream breakage:

- The caller requested an automotive product-engineering domain directive, but the rendered prompt omits all automotive-specific domain instructions.
- The manifest contains no explicit “requested domain variant file missing” error.
- Review models receive silently less-specific constraints, producing wrong or incomplete review behaviour.
- This is not caught by `_check_monotonicity()` because that checks the TOML policy, not whether the prose domain variant was loaded.
- The bug is especially dangerous because default loading without `variant` can still work, masking the failure until callers use the documented `domain_variant` API.

ANALYSE:  
Constraint classification: HARD — this is deterministic interface correctness. A documented variant-loading path must either load the requested existing variant or fail loudly; silently omitting the layer produces wrong results.

Premises:

1. `_load_domain_directive(domain, variant)` documents and implements variant-specific loading.
2. The repository contains valid domain files whose basename prefix is not equal to the directory name:
   - `product-engineering/product_automotive.txt`
   - `cross-domain/cross_software_hardware.txt`
3. The current implementation assumes the filename prefix is always exactly `domain`.
4. For `domain="product-engineering"` and `variant="automotive"`, the generated filename is `product-engineering_automotive.txt`.
5. That file does not exist, while `product_automotive.txt` does exist.
6. The function returns `None` instead of loading the existing unique matching variant.

Concrete trace:

```python
domain = "product-engineering"
variant = "automotive"
domain_dir = DIRECTIVES_DIR / "product-engineering"

constructed = domain_dir / f"{domain}_{variant}.txt"
# constructed = ".../product-engineering/product-engineering_automotive.txt"

constructed.exists() == False

actual = domain_dir / "product_automotive.txt"
actual.exists() == True

_load_domain_directive(domain, variant) == None
```

Formal conclusion:

Because `_load_domain_directive()` hardcodes `f"{domain}_{variant}.txt"` and does not search for an existing unique `*_{variant}.txt` file, valid domain variants are silently dropped for domains whose directory names and filename prefixes differ. CONFIRMED.

FIX:  
Use the exact current filename convention first, but fall back to a unique suffix match inside the domain directory. If no file or multiple files match, fail closed by returning `None` rather than guessing ambiguously.

The fix addresses the root cause: the assumption that directory name always equals filename prefix.

## Finding 1 — `_block_is_hard` over‑matches SOFT directives via case‑insensitive token check

**FINDING_ID:** F014  
**SEVERITY:** 0.60  
**FLAW_CLASS:** 5 (correctness)  
**ABSTRACTION_INDEX:** 0.25  

### FIND
The function `_block_is_hard` (line ~360) determines whether a directive block contains HARD-constraint language. It does so by uppercasing the entire block and then checking for sub‑string matches against `_HARD_BLOCK_MARKERS`:

```python
upper = f" {block.upper()} "
return any(m in upper for m in _HARD_BLOCK_MARKERS)
```

Because the search is case‑insensitive (via `.upper()`) and uses simple substring inclusion, **any** SOFT directive that contains the word “must”, “never”, “required”, “do not”, or “always” — in any original casing — will be misclassified as HARD. Example:

```
"You must provide a fix for CONFIRMED findings only."
```

This is a SOFT behavioural directive, yet `_block_is_hard` returns `True` because `" MUST "` appears in the uppercased string. The original code’s `_HARD_BLOCK_MARKERS` tuple contains `" MUST "`, `" NEVER "`, `" REQUIRED "`, `" DO NOT "`, `" ALWAYS "`, etc.

### FOLLOW
1. **Intra‑packet pruning** (`_prune_packet_directives`): blocks classified as HARD are never removed, even when the packet must be shrunk to meet the coherence budget. Over‑classified SOFT blocks therefore survive pruning and keep the directive text longer than necessary.
2. **Cross‑layer conflict resolution** (`resolve_layer_conflicts`): a directive incorrectly tagged as HARD wins against genuinely SOFT opponents that should have prevailed, distorting the conflict‑resolution priority.
3. **Coherence budget**: when over‑matching protects SOFT text from pruning, the final rendered prompt may exceed the model’s constraint‑density budget, degrading review quality.

### ANALYSE
**Premises:**
1. HARD‑block detection is used by the pruning and conflict‑resolution subsystems to enforce the coherence budget and to give HARD constraints precedence.
2. The detection must distinguish between explicitly marked HARD directives (e.g., `MUST`, `NEVER`) and SOFT prose that happens to contain the same words in lower‑case form.
3. The current implementation collapses this distinction, treating any occurrence of the marker sub‑strings (regardless of case) as HARD.

**Concrete trace:**  
A domain directive such as `"You must check the registry before filing new findings."` → uppercased → contains `" MUST "` → classified HARD → survives pruning even when the instruction is SOFT → budget may be violated.

**Classification:** SOFT — the pruning heuristic is inherently approximate, but this specific over‑reach degrades the composer’s ability to stay within budget. **CONFIRMED** by code inspection.

### FIX
Replace the case‑insensitive substring check with a word‑boundary‑aware regex that matches **only** the markers when they appear as **whole uppercase words** in the original (un‑uppercased) text. This preserves detection of genuine `MUST` / `NEVER` markers while ignoring lower‑case “must” or “never” used in ordinary prose.

def _prune_for_coherence(
    packets: list[DirectivePacket],
    policy: dict[str, Any],
    budget: float,
) -> tuple[list[DirectivePacket], list[str]]:
    """Prune SOFT content if constraint density exceeds budget.

    Two-pass strategy:
    1. Intra-packet pruning: remove individual SOFT directives within packets
    2. Whole-packet pruning: remove entire SOFT packets if still over budget

    HARD packets are NEVER pruned. Universal is NEVER pruned.
    """
    total_chars = sum(len(p.text) for p in packets)
    token_estimate = max(total_chars // 4, 1)
    constraint_count = _count_constraints(policy)
    density = constraint_count / token_estimate

    if density <= budget:
        return packets, []

    pruned_names: list[str] = []
    mutable_packets = list(packets)

    prunable = [
        (i, p) for i, p in enumerate(mutable_packets)
        if p.constraint_class == "SOFT" and p.layer != "universal"
    ]
    prune_order = {"situation": 0, "domain": 1, "phenotype": 2}
    prunable.sort(key=lambda x: prune_order.get(x[1].layer, 3))

    # Pass 1: intra-packet pruning — trim SOFT directives within each packet
    for idx, packet in prunable:
        target_chars = max(int(len(packet.text) * 0.7), 1)
        new_packet = _prune_packet_directives(packet, target_chars)
        if len(new_packet.text) < len(packet.text):
            mutable_packets[idx] = new_packet
            pruned_names.append(f"{packet.name}::intra")

        remaining_chars = sum(len(p.text) for p in mutable_packets)
        remaining_tokens = max(remaining_chars // 4, 1)
        density = constraint_count / remaining_tokens
        if density <= budget:
            return mutable_packets, pruned_names

    # Pass 2: whole-packet pruning if still over budget
    keep_indices = set(range(len(mutable_packets)))
    for idx, packet in prunable:
        keep_indices.discard(idx)
        pruned_names.append(packet.name)

        remaining = [mutable_packets[i] for i in sorted(keep_indices)]
        remaining_chars = sum(len(p.text) for p in remaining)
        remaining_tokens = max(remaining_chars // 4, 1)
        density = constraint_count / remaining_tokens
        if density <= budget:
            return remaining, pruned_names

    return [mutable_packets[i] for i in sorted(keep_indices)], pruned_names

    policy: dict[str, Any],

    The current density metric is policy_constraint_count / token_estimate.

    deleting packet text can make density worse. Therefore pruning candidates

        return constraint_count / tokens
